relationships.reason: The earlier optimized two-use equality for full-Choi-rank qubit channels is included in the later all-positive-integer-use theorem under the same fresh minimal environment, fixed full four-outcome measurement and recovery conventions. The all-n determinant-polarization result subsumes n=2.

The earlier finite-offset symmetric K3 weak-drive inequality and sharp factor 2 are the N=3 specialization of the later complete-K_N weak-Fourier-drive theorem. Neither proves a finite-amplitude phase bound. The earlier specialized calculation remains available.

Both use the same ordered GAD instrument, incoherent 03|12 bit, p=18/25, gamma=3/10 and two-use policy distinction. The later exact current-bit optimum 289/400 and history value 1831/2500 give 99/10000 advantage, strengthening the earlier 7/2500 witness, and add a certified rectangle. The n=1 equality also settles earliest onset.

Both concern two-copy binary-state entanglement of purification. big_mac proves pathwise positivity for every positive nonproduct binary table without a common neighborhood; small_mac proves a full U(16) strict local minimum modulo gauge at r=1/2. Neither recorded statement contains the other complete statement. Keep both, link them, and do not infer global additivity.

The small_mac result is an all-s certificate for q=1..6 one-hub subdivided stars. big_mac proves a full-gap, tail-controlled two-hub family for k>=100 in eta=theta/k, theta in [1/2,2]. Different topology, size and parameter quantifiers; neither is an all-graph proof.

The two-gene finite-RNA-lifetime matched-baseline theorem is not the three-species direct-abundance feedback-ring weak-regulation result. The intermediate RNA state, number of species, baseline and whole-space remainder are different.
A finite nonreciprocal full-current large-deviation counterexample is not the resource-dependent three-port noise/entropy theorem. The target bound, observable and hypothesis sets differ.
